welcome.label: Welcome · Around the Bend

parts.label: 🦆 The Duck Derby, part 2
parts.title: Now on Palmetto Creek
parts.body: The flowing creek will carry the ducks this time.

parts.label: 📻 The practice run
parts.title: “WAIT!” was heard as “…ready!”
parts.body: The walkies cut out. The waterfall drowned out shouting.

parts.label: ❓ The question
parts.title: What code should the judges use?
parts.body: And how will they know it works?

welcome.script:
(Cup your hands around your mouth like you’re yelling across a field.) Can you hear me over there? No? Hmm.

[ON SCREEN: The Duck Derby, part 2]
The Duck Derby moved to Palmetto Creek, where the water flows. Great idea!

[ON SCREEN: The practice run]
But at the practice run, the walkie-talkies cut out, and “Wait!” was heard as “ready!” The ducks floated right past an empty finish.

[ON SCREEN: The question]
Today you’ll help the judges design a code that can’t get mixed up. Dr. Nair’s case file is just below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · the secret knock (Clue 1)

parts.label: 🤔 Think about it
parts.title: What did it mean?
parts.body: Can you tell without the key?

warmup.script:
(Knock on your desk: knock-knock, pause, knock.) Did I just say something? What was it?

[ON SCREEN: The secret knock]
Someone is knocking on the clubhouse door. Listen, then tap the door to knock the same rhythm back.

[ON SCREEN: Think about it]
You copied it. But what does it mean? Look for the code key. Then write about a code you already know, like a doorbell or a school bell.

part1.label: Part 1 · the flashlight key + lighthouses (Clue 2)
part1.script:
(Turn a flashlight, or a phone light, on and off: short, short, short.) Short flashes. (Now hold it on longer.) A long flash.

[ON SCREEN: The flashlight key]
Tap the red key quickly for a dot. Hold it for a dash. Send SOS, the call for help. If a flash is in between, your partner can’t tell what you meant!

[ON SCREEN: A real lighthouse]
Then meet three lighthouses that each flash their own pattern. Can you tell them apart?

part2.label: Part 2 · which signal crosses the bend? (Clue 3)
part2.script:
(Hold up two fingers, then fold one down.) Goals are what a design must do. Limits are what it has to work around.

[ON SCREEN: Goals and limits]
Switch on each limit at the creek and watch the ways to send a message drop out. Then check the last one against every goal.

explore.label: Part 3 · test it across the creek (Clue 4)

parts.label: 📝 Test it across the creek
parts.title: Test, change one thing, test again

explore.script:
(Hold up one finger.) One. Engineers change ONE thing at a time. Why do you think that is?

[ON SCREEN: Test it across the creek]
Press Test across the creek and read the test sheet. Which messages did the partner mix up? Those are your failure points. Change just one thing, a pattern tile or the gap, and test again. Keep going until your partner reads all four. There’s more than one way to fix it!

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Which code should the judges use?
parts.body: Pick the plan that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Three places to work
rows: Invent your own code, then sketch its key

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. Which code should the judges use on race night? Pick the plan that fits every clue. Then watch for a twist on race night.

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Next: two short answers. For Part C, invent a code for your own life, like a family signal or a game with a friend. Sketch its key and label it. Last comes your CER.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “Real engineers design things right the first time. Testing is just for amateurs.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
(Pretend to crumple a paper and toss it.) First try, perfect? Hmm.

[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says real engineers get it right the first time. Think about the judges’ first test, and race night in the mist.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts. Then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…”

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🔦 Your specimen
parts.title: A judge’s signal flashlight
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next lesson
parts.title: What is matter?
parts.body: The stuff everything is made of.

closing.script:
(Flash a light twice.) Two flashes: case closed!

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and a judge’s signal flashlight goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next lesson]
Next time we start something new: matter, the stuff everything is made of. See you then!

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
